sentences.text: The customer is Gabriel Novak, age 64, a retired high-school teacher in Alameda, CA, and a customer since 1998-04-02.
On 2026-09-29 checking account ending 2954 received a $418,500.00 inbound wire from Bayside Title & Escrow (fictional).
On 2026-10-01 $400,000.00 moved to the customer's own brokerage account ending 8120.
The alert was detected on 2026-09-30, one day after the wire, with a filing decision due by 2026-10-30.
The wire came from a title and escrow company for the sale of 22 Linden Court, Alameda CA.
The settlement statement shows a sale price of $455,000.00, a mortgage payoff of $31,240.00, and fees of $5,260.00, leaving net proceeds of $418,500.00, which matches the wire.
Only one money-mule indicator fired, inflow 60.3 times the expected monthly activity, and no typology matched.
Funds arrived by a single domestic wire from the escrow agent and moved to the customer's own brokerage account at this bank, with no cash, third-party, or cross-border activity.

sample_draft.rationale: The large wire is explained by a documented home sale whose net proceeds of $418,500.00 match the wire, and the funds stayed in the customer's own accounts.
